archetypes.name: Evaluate an Exponential Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §6.1 — Exponential Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Evaluation substitutes the input into the exponent expression before applying exponent rules and multiplying by any initial value.
archetypes.mentalModel: Place the input into the function's exponent slot, simplify that exponent, evaluate the power, then apply the outside multiplier.

cognitiveTraps.description: Combining the leading coefficient with the base before evaluating the exponent.
Evaluating the base power without substituting the requested input into the exponent.

archetypes.figureNone: The task is exact symbolic evaluation; a figure adds no information needed to determine the output.

archetypes.name: Write an Exponential Rule from Data
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §6.1 — Exponential Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: An exponential rule has a fixed initial value and a constant multiplicative factor for each unit increase in the input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Use the value at input zero as the initial value; compare two outputs to recover the repeated multiplicative factor.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using an additive output change as the exponential base instead of a multiplicative ratio.
Treating the initial output as the growth factor.

archetypes.figureNone: The item provides exact symbolic input-output data; a figure is not needed to recover the rule.

archetypes.name: Apply a Compound Interest Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §6.1 — Exponential Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Compound interest multiplies the current balance by a fixed factor each compounding period.
archetypes.mentalModel: Convert the annual rate into a per-period rate, count the total periods, and apply the repeated multiplier to the initial principal.

cognitiveTraps.description: Adding a fixed interest amount each period instead of compounding the current balance.
Using elapsed years as the exponent when the account compounds multiple times per year.

archetypes.figureNone: The task is an exact finance calculation with a standard compounding relation; a figure would not clarify the computation.

archetypes.name: Evaluate a Natural Exponential Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §6.1 — Exponential Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: The natural exponential function uses the positive constant e as its base and follows the same substitution process as other exponential functions.
archetypes.mentalModel: Substitute the input into the exponent of e; if a numerical value is requested, evaluate e to that power with the stated precision.

cognitiveTraps.description: Treating e as a variable factor rather than a fixed mathematical constant.
Rounding an exponent before evaluating the exponential, changing the final value.

archetypes.figureNone: The requested output is a numerical function value; a figure contributes no additional reasoning.

archetypes.name: Apply Continuous Compounding
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §6.1 — Exponential Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Continuous compounding models instantaneous growth with base e raised to the product of annual rate and time.
archetypes.mentalModel: Convert the percentage rate to a decimal, multiply by elapsed time for the exponent of e, then scale by the initial principal.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using the percentage number directly as r in the exponent instead of dividing by 100.
Using linear growth P*(1+r*t) instead of continuous exponential growth P*e^(r*t).

archetypes.figureNone: The task evaluates a continuous growth formula numerically; a graph is not needed.
